why: The core tier is empty. 6.0 demoted the nineteen rules that declared it, because none of their 95% Wilson intervals cleared the 10% ceiling — the smallest observed ciHigh across 73 measured rules is 0.138, and a rule observing zero false positives needs n >= 35 to clear 0.1. The corpus is too small, not the ceiling too tight, so the baseline is zero and every promotion from here is governed by this ratchet. See docs/ANTI-CREEP.md.
howToMove: Set previousBaselineCore to the value you are replacing whenever you record a new baselineCore. The law compares the tier against previousBaselineCore, so lowering baselineCore to match a grown tier does NOT hide the growth. A tier bigger than previousBaselineCore needs an ANTI-CREEP-EXCEPTION line in the UNRELEASED CHANGELOG entry; a tier at or under it needs nothing.
